$comment: API list prices, USD per 1M tokens (proposal Screen D: 価格表はデータ). Copy to ~/.switchboard/pricing.json to override; the user file replaces this one. `billing` says whether a runner's usage is actually charged (api) or covered by a subscription (subscription → 実課金 0). Unknown models are reported as unpriced. Verified 2026-09-23 against the official pages: Anthropic platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing (cacheWrite = 5-minute cache write, 1.25x input; cacheWrite1h = the 1-hour cache write Claude Code uses, 2x input; Fable 5.1 cache reads are 0.025x input = $0.25, Opus 5.5 cache reads are 0.05x input = $0.20, all other Claude models 0.1x; Sonnet 5's $2/$10 introductory price became the standard price; Sonnet 5.5 keeps Sonnet 5's prices, checked 2026-09-29; Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50, cache reads $0.01, writes $0.125 (5m) / $0.20 (1h), checked 2026-10-07 — these are its prices for prompts up to 100K tokens; a prompt over 100K pays 5x on every field, and that tier is not modelled), OpenAI developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (standard tier; GPT-6.1 Sol $2/$10, cached input $0.10, cache writes $2.50, checked 2026-10-01; Luna/Terra list prices are standard, not promotional; Sol's $4/$20 is promotional through at least 2026-11-21; >272K-input requests bill 2x input / 1.5x output for the whole request and are not modelled; cacheWrite = 1.25x input, except gpt-5-nano, which does not charge cache writes), Google ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (paid tier; Gemini 3.7 Flash $0.75/$3.75/$0.075 is introductory through 2026-12-31 and doubles on 2027-01-01 — in the table as a dated change (`changes`: each entry is valid from 00:00 UTC of `from`, fields left out keep the row's value, usage is priced at the time it happened; cacheWrite1h is not derived from cacheWrite, so a change that moves the write prices must repeat cacheWrite1h); Gemini charges cache storage per hour, not per written token, so cacheWrite is 0; Gemini 3.1 Pro's >200K tier is not modelled).
